# archimedes-server

> Backend service that ingests MQTT tank/pump events, computes tank volume from geometry, persists to PostgreSQL, and exposes a read-only HTTP API.

## Overview

Archimedes-server subscribes to two MQTT topics: one carrying water tank sensor distance readings, the other carrying pump start/stop events. It converts each tank reading into a volume using the tank's registered shape and dimensions, writes the result to PostgreSQL, and records pump run history. A separate HTTP server exposes everything it has stored through read-only endpoints. The codebase follows a hexagonal layout: `core/` holds domain types, interfaces, and use cases with no dependency on any concrete adapter; `adapters/` implements those interfaces against PostgreSQL, MQTT, HTTP, and file logging.

## Key Concepts

- **Tank**: a physical water tank with an ID, name, and a stored shape/dimensions used to compute volume from a sensor distance reading.
- **Pump**: a physical pump whose start/stop events are recorded as a history of runs (`PumpStatus`), each with a start time and, once stopped, a stop time and reason.
- **IVolumeCalculator**: the abstraction for converting a sensor distance into a fluid volume for a given tank shape. `cylindrical_cone` is the only implementation today.
- **IProcessStream**: the abstraction a stream consumer calls with a raw MQTT message body; implemented separately for tank and pump events.

## API Reference

### Core Types

- `core/tank/domain.Tank`, `core/tank/domain.TankStatus` — tank identity and latest volume reading.
- `core/pump/domain.Pump`, `core/pump/domain.PumpStatus` — pump identity and one run (start/stop) record.
- `core/volume/domain.Shape` — tank shape identifier stored in PostgreSQL (`cylindrical_cone`).
- `core/processor/domain.WaterTankEvent`, `core/processor/domain.PumpEvent` — the JSON payloads carried on the MQTT topics.

### Core Interfaces

- `core/tank/interfaces.IReadTank` / `IUpdateTank` — read and write tank data.
- `core/pump/interfaces.IReadPumpStatus` / `IUpdatePumpStatus` — read and write pump run data.
- `core/volume/interfaces.IGetVolumeType` — resolve a tank's `IVolumeCalculator` from its stored shape.
- `core/volume/interfaces.IVolumeCalculator` — compute a volume from a sensor distance reading.
- `core/processor/interfaces.IProcessStream` — handle one raw MQTT message.

### HTTP Endpoints (adapters/endpoint/http)

- `GET /health` — liveness check.
- `GET /read/tank` — list tanks.
- `GET /read/tank/{id}` — a tank's latest status.
- `GET /read/pump` — list pumps.
- `GET /read/pump/{id}` — a pump's most recent run.
- `GET /read/pump/{id}/historic` — a pump's full run history.

## Common Patterns

### Adding a new tank shape

Implement `core/volume/interfaces.IVolumeCalculator` in a new package under `core/volume/usecases/`, then register the shape's `domain.Shape` value in `adapters/database/postgresql.getVolumeType.GetVolumeFromShape`'s switch statement.

### Adding a new MQTT-driven use case

Implement `core/processor/interfaces.IProcessStream`, wire a new `adapters/stream/mqtt.NewStreamConsumer` in `main.go` pointed at the relevant topic, and start it on its own goroutine alongside the existing tank/pump consumers.
